newsitem.title: japan: TIFFE Euroyen ends slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends slightly higher.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen futures on TIFFE ended slightly higher on Tuesday.

The Bank of Japan's decision to adopt an accommodative money market stance this morning helped ease the market's concerns about a possible near-term change in the BOJ's monetary policy, and contributed to a rise in Euroyen futures, a trader for a major brokerage house said.
The December's turnover during the day session was 62,818 contracts.
The BOJ refrained from conducting its regular money market operation this morning, which left the market with a fund surplus of about 120 billion yen.
The central bank's accommodative stance led to an easing in the key overnight call rate, traders said.
Traders said the weighted average of the key overnight call rate was likely to be 0.53 percent on Tuesday, down from Monday's weighted average of 0.57 percent.
The BOJ will probably conduct an accommodative operation on Wednesday, a regional bank trader said.
"If the BOJ reverts to a neutral stance, the overnight call rate might rise as high as 0.60 percent," the trader said.
The key three-month certificates of deposit rate rose to 0.60 percent on Tuesday, its highest level since August 20, 1996, traders said.

The rise in the key CD rate was due to a rise in short-term rates in general ahead of corporate book-closings at the end of March, and a view held by some market players that the BOJ may raise interest rates earlier than expected, traders said.

"Earlier, the widely held view was that it would take at least until September to evaluate the condition of the economy's recovery...but a view is beginning to emerge that the BOJ may make a decision on whether to raise interest rates after the release of the key 'tankan' survey in July," a city bank trader said.

The market will be focusing near-term on the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee meeting to take place later in the day, and on BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita's news conference on Wednesday, traders said.
